questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Rahul knows Shahbaz since childhood.

options.text: Shahbaz was known to Rahul since childhood.
Shahbaz is known to Rahul since childhood.
Shahbaz known by Rahul since childhood.
Shahbaz has known Rahul since childhood.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Shahbaz is known to Rahul since childhood.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice means that the subject of the sentence is not performing the action, but rather receiving it.
 
 
• She was attacked by a stranger.
 
 
 
• To convert a sentence into passive voice:
 
 
• the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence
 
• and the verb is changed to a passive form (usually "to be" + past participle).
 
 
 
• **In this case, "Shahbaz" is the object of the active sentence, so it becomes the subject of the passive sentence ("Shahbaz is known"), and the verb "knows" is changed to its passive form "is known".**
 
• **The preposition "since childhood" remains the same in both active and passive voice.**
 
• Thus, the sentence in passive form will be: 
 
 
• Shahbaz is known to Rahul since childhood.
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, "Shahbaz was known to Rahul since childhood," is in passive voice but uses the wrong tense (past simple instead of present simple).
 
• Option 3, "Shahbaz known by Rahul since childhood," is missing the auxiliary verb "is" to form a complete passive sentence.
 
• Option 4, "Shahbaz has known Rahul since childhood," is in active voice and does not use the correct subject-verb-object order for a passive sentence.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The shopman was very interested in selling this creamy box to her as he would gain a big margin.

B. The man on the counter showed her 'an exquisite little enamel box' with a very fine glaze as if baked in cream.

C. As the box was too expensive, priced twenty - eight guineas, she asked the shopkeeper to keep it for her.

D. She went inside a little antique shop in Curzon Street. This was the usual shop where the shopkeeper was ridiculously fond of serving her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**DBAC.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph is about a woman visiting an antique shop and being shown an expensive enamel box by the shopkeeper.
 
 
• **Thus, the introducing sentence will be sentence D. It will be followed by the sentence B.**
 
 
 
• Further, the shopman is eager to sell the box as he would make a big profit.
 
 
• Thus, sentence A will follow sentence B.
 
 
 
• The woman cannot afford the box but asks the shopkeeper to keep it for her.
 
 
• Therefore, sentence C will come at the end of the passage.
 
 
 
• The paragraph is arranged in chronological order, starting with the woman entering the shop and ending with her asking the shopkeeper to keep the box.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:

The plants are not be watered by them.

- To change it to passive voice, we need to make the object (the plants) the subject and use the passive form of the verb ("will be watered").
- The preposition "by" is used to indicate who is performing the action (in this case, "them").
- The negative "not" stays in the same position in the sentence.

Additional Information:
- Option 2 ("The plants will not be watered by us") changes the subject to "us" instead of "them."
- Option 3 ("The plants are not be watered by them") has an incorrect verb form ("are" instead of "will be").
- Option 4 ("They shall not water the plants") is in active voice and does not use the passive form of the verb.
- Option 5 is blank.
